note: MissionMed-original prompts for Request-a-Story guest contributors. Written for people who are NOT writers: one concrete memory cue each, answerable out loud in under two minutes, no assumed literacy register, no US-centric anchors, no trauma pressure. Every prompt addresses the contributor as 'you' and the student by first name ({name}). Synthesized from the B1-513 research principles (episodic cueing, ordinary moments, one question at a time); no proprietary question banks copied.

prompts.text: What is the first moment you remember thinking — this child is going to take care of people?
prompts.hint: One moment is enough. Where were you? What did {name} do?

prompts.text: Tell about a time {name} surprised you when they were young — something you still bring up at the dinner table.
prompts.hint: Say it the way you'd tell it to a friend.

prompts.text: What did {name} do as a child when someone in the house was sick?
prompts.hint: Even a small thing — a glass of water, a drawing, sitting close.

prompts.text: What is something {name} refused to give up on, no matter how hard it got? Tell about one specific time.
prompts.hint: What did you see them do that week?

prompts.text: Was there ever a moment {name} taught YOU something? What happened?
prompts.hint: Parents learn from children too — those stories are gold.

prompts.text: Tell about a meal or dish that means something in your family — and what {name} has to do with it.
prompts.hint: Who cooks it? When? What does {name} always do?

prompts.text: What is a story about {name} that you two still laugh about — the one that comes up every time you're together?
prompts.hint: Tell it exactly the way you tell it at home.

prompts.text: Tell about a time {name} stood up for you — or for someone else — when it wasn't easy.
prompts.hint: What was happening? What did they say or do?

prompts.text: What was {name} like when things went wrong at home? Tell about one specific day you remember.
prompts.hint: Little moments say a lot.

prompts.text: What did {name} love doing as a kid that nobody outside the family knows about?
prompts.hint: A hobby, an obsession, a game they invented…

prompts.text: Tell about a moment you watched {name} with a patient, a stranger, or someone who needed help — and felt proud.
prompts.hint: Where were you? What exactly did they do?

prompts.text: What does {name} do after a hard day that most people never see?
prompts.hint: The quiet routines say the most.

prompts.text: Tell the story of a sacrifice you watched {name} make for their path in medicine — one specific season or day.
prompts.hint: What did it cost? What kept them going?

prompts.text: What do you remember about {name} as a small child that already showed who they would become?
prompts.hint: One afternoon, one visit, one little scene is perfect.

prompts.text: Is there something you taught {name} — a saying, a skill, a way of doing things — that you hope they carry with them?
prompts.hint: Tell about the day you taught it.

prompts.text: Tell about a time {name} helped you — with your health, your home, or just your day — without being asked.
prompts.hint: What did they notice that others didn't?

prompts.text: What is {name} like at family gatherings? Tell about one gathering you still remember because of them.
prompts.hint: A wedding, a holiday, an ordinary Sunday…

prompts.text: Tell about an adventure — big or small — that you and {name} had growing up.
prompts.hint: Where were you? What almost went wrong?

prompts.text: Tell about the moment you knew {name} was going to be your friend for life.
prompts.hint: One scene — where were you, what happened?

prompts.text: When you needed someone — really needed someone — what did {name} do? Tell about that time.
prompts.hint: Share only what feels comfortable to share.

prompts.text: What is something {name} does for other people that they would never mention about themselves?
prompts.hint: Tell about one time you saw it happen.

prompts.text: What were you two obsessed with as kids? Tell about one day of it.
prompts.hint: Games, plans, schemes — the sillier, the better.

prompts.text: Tell about a time young {name} got in trouble — or got you BOTH in trouble — and what it showed about them.
prompts.hint: Funny is welcome here.

prompts.text: Tell about a night before an exam, a brutal rotation week, or a moment of doubt — and what {name} did that you still remember.
prompts.hint: One specific night or day.

prompts.text: What is {name} like at 3 a.m. on call — the version of them patients and professors never quite see?
prompts.hint: A moment, a habit, a phrase they always say.

prompts.text: Tell about a time the group was struggling and {name} changed the mood or the plan.
prompts.hint: What exactly did they say or do first?

prompts.text: Among the many students you've taught, tell about one moment {name} did something that made you remember them.
prompts.hint: One class, one question, one patient encounter.

prompts.text: Tell about a time {name} handled feedback or failure in a way that impressed you.
prompts.hint: What was the situation, and what did they do next?

prompts.text: Was there a moment you saw {name} do the right thing when no one required it? Tell that story.
prompts.hint: Quiet integrity makes the best stories.

prompts.text: Tell about the conversation with {name} you still think about.
prompts.hint: Where were you? What did they ask or say?

prompts.text: How has {name} changed since you first met them? Tell about one moment that showed the change.
prompts.hint: First impression versus a recent moment works well.

prompts.text: Tell about a shift, a project, or a day when you were glad {name} was the one next to you.
prompts.hint: What happened, and what did they do?

prompts.text: What does {name} do when the plan falls apart? Tell about one time you watched it happen.
prompts.hint: Deadlines, emergencies, chaos — pick one.

prompts.text: Tell about a task you gave {name} that they handled in a way you didn't expect.
prompts.hint: What did you ask for — and what did they actually do?

prompts.text: If another employer called you about {name}, what one story would you tell them? Tell it now.
prompts.hint: The story, not the adjectives.

prompts.text: Tell about a game, match, or performance where {name} showed who they are.
prompts.hint: A win, a loss, or a moment in between.

prompts.text: When {name} lost at something, what did they do next? Tell about one time.
prompts.hint: How people lose says more than how they win.

prompts.text: Tell about a tradition, holiday, or journey in your family — and the part {name} always plays in it.
prompts.hint: What would be missing if {name} weren't there?

prompts.text: Tell about a moment {name} made you laugh so hard you still smile thinking about it.
prompts.hint: Set the scene — where were you, who else was there?

prompts.text: Tell about a time {name} showed up for you or for someone else — when they didn't have to.
prompts.hint: One specific day. What did they actually do?

prompts.text: What is something about {name} that you wish the people deciding their future knew? Tell the story that proves it.
prompts.hint: Not a list of qualities — one story.

prompts.text: Tell about an ordinary day with {name} that you'd love to live one more time.
prompts.hint: Nothing dramatic needed — ordinary is perfect.

prompts.text: Tell about a time you watched {name} fail at something — and what they did afterward.
prompts.hint: Only if you're comfortable — these often become their best stories.

prompts.text: What does {name} believe in? Tell about one moment you watched them act on it.
prompts.hint: Actions, not descriptions.

prompts.text: Tell about the first time you met {name} — what happened, and what did you think?
prompts.hint: First impressions make great openings.

prompts.text: What phrase or saying does {name} repeat all the time? Tell about the last time you heard them say it.
prompts.hint: Family catchphrases carry whole histories.

prompts.text: Tell about a moment {name} asked you a question that showed you how they think.
prompts.hint: The question itself, and where it led.

prompts.text: If you had to explain who {name} is using only one story from before medicine, which story would you tell?
prompts.hint: Take your time. Start with where it happened.
